coverage: overnight, since the evening edition (~19:45 to 08:20 CEST)
headline: Hackers heat up the fridges in 400+ French supermarkets and may have reached other EU countries; the IMF warns of an AI-driven correction as Korea’s chip stocks crash; xAI folds Cursor into one “X Subscription”; Germany’s digital minister wants to tax AI revenue.

stories.title: Hackers heat up supermarket fridges across France, and the attack may reach further into Europe
facts: From Sunday night, attackers remotely triggered forced defrost cycles in store refrigeration systems, heating fridges and freezers to as much as 50 °C for about six hours (AFP, Reuters).
Retailers report 400+ stores hit: Intermarché/Netto about 150–300, Coopérative U 100+, Carrefour 80, about 5% of Monoprix’s ~490 stores, plus several E. Leclerc branches.
Stock was thrown out, and the Paris prosecutor reports fires at some sites. Coopérative U’s CEO called the attack “unprecedented”.

The targeted controllers are reportedly from Danish supplier Danfoss. Intermarché says outdated, remotely reachable consoles were hit, and Danfoss points to old firmware and end-of-life AK-SM800/AK-SC355 units.

France’s cyber agency ANSSI is investigating with European partners. Sekoia says Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium were also affected. Ahold Delhaize took its refrigeration systems offline but sees no link.
EU food commissioner Christophe Hansen says food security needs “more attention at all levels”.
stories.whyItMatters: This is one of the clearest cases yet of a cyberattack causing physical damage across a whole sector at once: internet-reachable maintenance panels became a single point of failure for the cold chain. German confirmation is still missing, so check whether local chains run the same controllers.

image.alt: Intermarche was one of the groups affected — Gabriel BOUYS / AFP

stories.title: IMF warns of an AI-driven market correction as Korea’s chip stocks crash
facts: The IMF’s Global Financial Stability Report names three near-term risks: an AI-driven market correction, another jump in government bond yields, and cyberattacks.
It cites “growing evidence” that AI may need less investment, or pay off less, than expected. Hyperscalers now make up 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from under 1% in 2024.
The IMF slightly raised its world growth forecast, assuming oil averages $96 a barrel. For Germany it now expects 1.3% growth in 2026 (from 0.7%) and 1.1% in 2027.

South Korea’s Kospi lost up to 7.4% on Tuesday, dropping below 6,000 to its lowest level since late July. Samsung fell ~8% and SK hynix ~9–11%, and a sell-side sidecar halted program selling for 5 minutes.
The trigger was China’s CXMT saying it will bring next-gen server DRAM this year, after Micron fell 3.9% on Wall Street on Monday.
stories.whyItMatters: The warning came with a real-time demonstration: memory chips, the most AI-leveraged corner of the market, sold off hard on a single supply headline. Watch whether Europe’s chip names and the US open follow.

image.alt: International Monetary Fund chief economist Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas participates in a news conference. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images

stories.title: xAI bundles Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one “X Subscription”
facts: New tiers: Free, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100 and Ultra $200 a month. Premium covers what SuperGrok, Cursor Pro and X Premium+ did, which together cost $90.
Paid plans share one weekly-refreshing usage pool across Grok and Cursor, with at least 2× the coding usage of the comparable Cursor plan.
Third-party models (e.g. Claude, GPT) stay available in Cursor on Premium and above, but are billed separately at API list prices via top-ups.
Team seats cost the same as individual plans and include SSO, admin controls and SOC 2. xAI says that is cheaper per seat than old Cursor Teams, with 3× the coding usage.
Existing SuperGrok, Cursor and X Premium plans continue for now. Switching gives a prorated refund, and old plans are closed to new sign-ups.
stories.whyItMatters: For anyone paying for Cursor, the default economics now favour xAI’s own models: included usage applies to Grok models, while other vendors’ models are pay-as-you-go.

stories.title: Anthropic says new defences cut model-distillation harvesting by 90–99%
facts: Anthropic says its new measures cut the data that distillers harvest from Claude by about 90–99%, and extracted reasoning tokens by 10–100×.
“Preserved thinking” (Claude Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5) stops API accounts created on or after Aug 31, 2026 from editing Claude’s prior context. That makes proxy-network extraction harder.
A two-stage classifier blocks extraction attempts. Anthropic says it is about as robust as its bioweapons safeguards, with under 0.1% false positives.
Tens of thousands of accounts were banned. Anthropic names China’s Z.ai (Zhipu) as having tried to distil Claude while building GLM-5.3.
Trade-offs: some developers have to update their integrations.
stories.whyItMatters: Distillation is now treated like a misuse category, not just a terms-of-service issue. Expect more of the reasoning-visibility limits that developers have been noticing.

stories.title: Digital minister Wildberger wants to tax AI revenue in Germany
facts: Karsten Wildberger (CDU) told Tagesspiegel that the “extrem hohen Umsatz” (extremely high revenue) from AI must be taxed, with the money paying for reshaping the job market.
His argument: “Wenn hierzulande Wachstum und Wertschöpfung entstehen, müssen hierzulande auch Steuern gezahlt werden” (if growth and value are created here, taxes have to be paid here).
He would spend it on retraining and new jobs, e.g. in skilled trades and care. He expects more jobs long term, but different ones.
He is revisiting the idea behind a basic income as a response to AI-driven job change, but no longer wants to use the term.
So far there is no concrete tax design or draft law.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s a first from a sitting federal digital minister, and it lands the same day as the IMF warning about AI valuations. Expect pushback from his own party’s economic wing and the industry.

stories.title: Germany detains two Turkish nationals over the sabotage of a Starlink station in Poland
facts: Poland says German authorities detained two Turkish citizens suspected of setting fire to a Starlink ground station near Grójec on Sept 23.
The fire damaged the station’s power system and backup generator. Poland calls it sabotage aimed at disrupting internet services, including Ukraine’s military communications.
Polish officials say Russian intelligence was behind it. The suspects are awaiting transfer to Poland under European arrest warrants.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s another case of Russia-linked sabotage run through hired proxies, this time with the arrests made in Germany.

image.alt: The Starlink photo is seen on a mobile device with Ukraine on a map in the background in this illustration photo in Warsaw, Poland on 21 September, 2022.

facts.text: Trump defends his Russian diesel deal (“I made the right choice”) after seven senators, including Republicans Collins, Murkowski, Tillis and Curtis, demanded he reverse it.
Memory crunch: Counterpoint says global smartphone shipments fell 20% year on year in Q3, the lowest level since 2012. Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo were down 20–30%.

Getty Images will go private through Chapter 11, backed by $533m from the Getty family and Koch Equity Development. The restructuring is due by year-end, with no change to contributor payments announced so far.
Pope Leo XIV checks into Rome’s Gemelli hospital today. Surgery to remove the lung nodule is expected this afternoon or Wednesday morning.
RJ Mitte (Walt Jr. on “Breaking Bad”, a disability-rights advocate) has died at 34 in Brownsville, Texas. Police say the cause is undetermined and they suspect no foul play.
SpaceX CRS-35: Falcon 9 is targeting today at 12:33 Berlin to resupply the ISS (backup Wed 12:08). Dragon is due to dock Thursday around 17:00.
French YC startup HyLight raised €13m (~$14.5m) for autonomous hydrogen airships that inspect power lines and pipelines. It targets 15 airships by 2027 and expansion into Germany.
Codex CLI 0.157.0 starts a persistent, self-updating `app-server` daemon by default and copies ~374 MB of binaries into `~/.codex`. Issue #48195 asks for opt-in, and it hit 520 points on HN.
GitLab patched CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE in self-managed CE/EE. Upgrade to 19.4.2, 19.3.4 or 19.2.8; GitLab.com is already fixed.
SvelteKit merged #17398: CSP config now accepts the `report-sha256`/`report-sha384`/`report-sha512` keywords.
Bun merged #45099, fixing a startup SIGILL on Linux arm64 machines that report SVE2 without SVE.
Read: Daniel Lemire on parsing JSON at tens of gigabytes per second from Python.
